children: Wall Street ended the week in the red after a nearly 20-basis-point jump in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield
and the latest consumer price index inflation report landing.
U.S. Treasury yields
across the curve this week, with the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (
) climbing nearly 20 basis points to 4.97%. U.S.
rose 0.4% M/M in August, matching Wall Street estimates and accelerating from July’s 0.1% gain, according to Friday’s Bureau of Labor Statistics data release.
S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) decreased 1.10% week-over-week to 276.41 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF
was down 1.16% to $43.42.
The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index declined 1.06%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index retreated 1.14%.
Among largecap stocks, CBRE Group
led the decliners with a 5.53% retreat to $140.51. The week saw industrial REIT Lineage
file a civil lawsuit in Los Angeles against CBRE subsidiary Pearce Services over negligence in a fire incident.
KE Holdings
followed, falling 5.47% from the prior week to close at $16.93.
BXP
(-5.17% W/W to $64.70) was the next on the list. The stock was losing ahead of its presentation at the BofA Securities 2026 Global Real Estate Conference.
Host Hotels & Resorts

(+1.14% W/W to $22.24) was a gainer in the category. The stock found a place in Deutsche's 'buy the dip' list in leisure. Deutsche Bank sees ~31% upside to its HST price target, with a view that the pullback across lodging REITs was overdone relative to cruise lines.
Fermi
(+13.17% W/W to $5.50) topped the midcap gainers. The stock extended gains from the prior week when it saw call volume above normal and directionally bullish.

The feud between the company's board and its ousted former CEO Toby Neugebauer saw a new development this week. The founder parties filed a formal proposal for an independent strategic review of extraordinary transactions.
Opendoor Technologies
led the midcap losers, retreating 10.86% week-over-week to $2.79.

The week saw Opendoor CEO Kaz Nejatian say a sharp late-August housing downturn slowed its home sales and kept delistings high. As a result, the company's profit timeline has been pushed back by six to eight weeks.
Medical Properties Trust
(-9.90% W/W to $3.64) was also a significant decliner. MPT was among the most shorted stocks on the Wall Street at the beginning of the month.
Centerspace
(+11.26% W/W to $58.29) was the winner among smallcap stocks. Shares of the apartment REIT were rising after an announcement of an all-stock merger with Independence Realty Trust
in a deal valued at ~$8.1B.
Real REMAX

followed with a 10.22% advance to $20.28. This week, the company announced the addition of Clayton Coastal Group, which brings 37 agents to Real, expands its presence across Florida, and sets the stage for the team's expansion into New York, serving all five boroughs.
Redwood Trust

was a notable loser. The stock was down 20.76% week-over-week to $3.55 on the announcement of an upsized private offering of $185M aggregate principal amount of 7.00% convertible senior notes due 2030.
